**Finding: deviation (Section 13.5 Ownership, ¶p0115–p0116)**

- **Issue:** Section 13.5 correctly gives Corio ownership of Developments (interface coding/programs created solely by Corio) and has Commerce One assign any competing claim — but the "unless such Developments are supported on an ongoing basis by Commerce One in which case Commerce One will retain all ownership rights" carve-out flips ownership of our own work product to the Vendor with no licence back. That is an assignment of Customer IP to the Vendor, failing both the preferred and fallback positions.
- **Redline (validated, ok:true):** delete the carve-out so the sentence reads "…shall be owned by Corio, including all intellectual property rights in the Developments." Commerce One's pre-existing materials and its Software ownership under Section 2.8 are untouched; a support licence to Commerce One is offered as the fallback.
- **Noted, not flagged:** the last sentence of 13.5 defers ownership of Software enhancements to later negotiation, and there is no Customer Data ownership sentence (no Customer Data construct exists in this hosting licence).
